systems.platform: web-based data reception platform for Meteosat Third Generation data

note: The newsletter reports a DCCMS forecaster certified at a regional PUMA 2025/MTG training in Nairobi, but states no Malawian receiving station, data stream or use in DCCMS forecasts or warnings.

facts.fact: DCCMS says it completed installation of the PUMA 2025 satellite reception system at its Blantyre headquarters, replacing PUMA 2015 and giving access to Meteosat Third Generation products.

note: The document describes an AI weather model pilot and does not state satellite data reception or use.

facts.fact: Malawi's Department of Climate Change and Meteorological Services piloted the WFP-developed PRISM tool in five districts, which DCCMS officials say integrates satellite imagery with rainfall, soil moisture and vegetation indices to give real-time drought insight.
facts.system: PRISM (Platform for Real-time Impact and Situation Monitoring)

note: Document covers GBON surface and upper-air weather observation stations; no satellite data use for farming or forecasting and no consultation on a digital law or policy is stated.

facts.fact: The African Union Commission's ClimSA deck lists Malawi among 41 of 49 member states with a PUMA station installed as at 12 May 2026; the station carries satellite imagery.

Malawi's Department of Climate Change and Meteorological Services says it uses the Flash Flood Guidance System, which integrates satellite rainfall estimates with ground observations and hydrological models, to produce real-time flash flood risk maps.

Malawi's Department of Climate Change and Meteorological Services says it issues flash flood warnings generated with tools including the Flash Flood Guidance System, which uses satellite rainfall estimates.
